# <span id="aanchor317"></span> Exception Description Editor

Accessing this screen requires **Application Process – FLOWCAL Options** privileges.

Exceptions flag suspect data that has been imported or manually added to a meter, location, source, or ticket. Running validations for a meter after data has been added can also create exceptions.

Use the Exception Description Editor to update exception descriptions, set the severity level for an exception, or specify contacts to notify when an exception is generated.

<div class="procedure">

To access the Exception Description Editor:

1.  Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**.

2.  Select **Exception Description** within the **Application** group.

3.  Select an exception and click **Edit**.

4.  Edit the exception description data as needed.

    Only the description and severity are available for editing.

5.  Click **Save**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 551;height: 345;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Exception Description Screen Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Exception Description Screen Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Exception Description Screen Details">

The following items are available on the Exception Description Editor screen:

- **Number** - Unique numeric identifier associated with the exception

- **Description** - The actual exception text explaining the issue and cause

- **Severity** - The priority level defined for the exception; severity levels can range from 1 to 5 (example: 1 could be a normal exception, whereas a 5 could be a critical exception)

  The Severity setting is application-wide and requires services to be restarted. Setting the severity to "0" will disable the exception for the entire application. Updating exception severity will generate system message 1201 "Exception severity changed".

- **Object** - The type of device or object

- **Notify** - Contact types to notify when the specified exceptions are generated

  Existing contact types can be defined for each exception. As exceptions are generated, the contact(s) specified for the device Contact Type will be alerted by email when the exception is generated.

  <div class="example">

  <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example</a>

  Jane Doe is defined as Contact Type - Analyst for Meter 5555 within the Meter Editor. In the Exception Description Editor, the Contact Type - Analyst has been configured for Exception Number 12. Anytime exception 12 is generated for Meter 5555, Jane Doe will receive an email alert.

  </div>

- **Edit Criteria button** - This button is only visible when the user selects exceptions 6501-6600. (See: <a href="#CriteriaEditor" class="InlineLink">Exception Criteria Editor</a>)

The "Disable Exception 'Ignore' when Severity \>" setting on the FLOWCAL Configuration screen can be used to prevent users from acknowledging exceptions with a severity level greater than the level specified. By default, all exceptions have a severity of 1. Setting the severity level of an exception to be greater than the severity level set in FLOWCAL Configuration prevents users from being able to acknowledge that exception. This is useful if there are certain exceptions that should always require user intervention to resolve the exception, rather than just acknowledging it, such as no product on a batch.

</div>

<span id="CriteriaEditor"></span><a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Exception Criteria Editor">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Exception Criteria Editor</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Exception Criteria Editor">

When processing import data, FLOWCAL checks for string events, user string events or string alarms. If any are detected, FLOWCAL checks to see if any of the user-defined String Event and Alarm (SEA) exceptions (6501 - 6600) have a severity rating greater than 0 and are defined for the corresponding item. If so, the string field from the event or alarm is checked against the defined exception criteria. If it is met, an exception is generated and attached to the periodic record time frame that encompasses the alarm or event.

Use the Exception Criteria Editor to define parameters that will trigger the generation of SEA exceptions.

<div class="procedure">

To access the Exception Criteria Editor and set criteria:

1.  Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**.
2.  Select **Exception Description** within the **Application** group.
3.  Select an exception number from 6501 to 6600.
4.  Click the **Edit Criteria** button.
5.  Click **Edit**.
6.  Enter the exception text in the **Description** field.
7.  Select the type of criteria that will trigger the exception (example: "Event Contains:").
8.  Click **Add** to add a new criterion.
9.  Enter the conditions that must be met for the exception to be generated. These definitions allow for operators AND, OR, or NOT, as well as wildcard operators.
10. Click the **Clear** button to remove all criteria if desired.
11. Click **Validate** for FLOWCAL to verify that your changes are correct.
12. Click **Save**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 564;height: 382;" />

</div>

</div>
